content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity apps and re-implementing them faithfully in SwiftUI for a new product. You think in tokens, not vibes: every color, radius and spacing value you output is a named constant, never a magic number typed inline.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from monday.com's iOS visual language — use these as ground truth, don't invent substitutes:

COLOR ROLES
- Canvas: white #FFFFFF (light) / deep indigo #181B34 (dark, NOT neutral black)
- Surfaces (dark): #20243F (surface 1), #292F4C (surface 2, hovered rows)
- Dividers: #E6E9F0 (light) / #353B5C (dark)
- Text: #323338 (primary light) / #F5F6F8 (primary dark), #676879 (secondary light) / #A7AFC6 (secondary dark)
- Action color: Primary Blue #0073EA (pressed #0060C2) — the ONLY interactive/CTA color
- Multicolor data palette (full-bleed fills, never tints): Red/Stuck #E2445C, Orange/Working #FDAB3D, Green/Done #00C875, Bright Blue #579BFC, Purple #A25DDC, Dark Purple #401694, Indigo #5559DF, Yellow #FFCB00 (dark text #323338), Teal #00D2D2 (dark text), Pink #FF158A, Bright Green #9CD326 (dark text), Navy/Not-started #333D6E

TYPE LADDER — Figtree (fallback: -apple-system/SF Pro), weights 400/500/600/700/800, no thin:
- Screen Title 32pt/800, Board Title 26pt/700, Group Header 22pt/800 (rendered IN the group's own hue), Section 18pt/700, Body 16pt/400, Item Name 14pt/500, Column Header 13pt/600, Status Label 11pt/700 (often uppercased), Tab Label 10pt/600

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; scale 4/6/8/10/12/14/18/22/24/32/40/56
- Radius scale: 0pt (grid lines), 4pt (status/priority cells, battery bar), 6-8pt (buttons, search), 12pt (sheets/modals), 999pt (pills, FAB), 50% (avatars)
- Item row height ~48pt; 6pt group-color stripe runs the FULL row height flush to the leading edge (0 inset)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Full-bleed status cell — a solid saturated rounded-rect (4pt radius) filling its whole grid cell, white (or dark on yellow/teal/bright-green) uppercase 11pt/700 text — never a small tint chip
2. Group-color stripe — a 6pt vertical bar of the group's assigned hue on every item row's leading edge
3. Battery rollup — a 24pt segmented horizontal bar (4pt radius) proportional to a group's status mix, animating width on change (250ms ease-out)
4. View switcher — Main Table / Kanban / Timeline / Calendar / Chart tabs rendering the same underlying items, active tab gets a 2.5pt blue underline
5. Person cell — 24pt circular avatars overlapping -6pt when stacked, "+N" overflow chip
6. FAB — 56pt blue circle, tinted blue shadow rgba(0,115,234,0.45) 0 8px 20px (never a gray shadow)
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Status and priority are ALWAYS full-bleed solid fills, never 12-16% tint chips — this is what separates monday.com's board from Asana-style restraint; a tint chip here is a defect, not a stylistic choice.
2. Every item row carries its group-color stripe flush to the leading edge with zero inset — if the stripe has a gap or margin, it stops reading as the board's structural spine.
3. Blue (#0073EA) is reserved exclusively for actions (FAB, CTAs, active tab, links) — never repurpose it as a data/status color, and never use a data color (red/green/orange) as a primary CTA.
4. Dark mode uses the indigo #181B34, never pure black — and the multicolor status palette must stay fully saturated and IDENTICAL in dark mode; status colors never dim, because color carries the meaning.
5. Group headers render in their own group color at 22pt/800 — a plain-black group header is a compliance bug, not a simplification.
6. Keep the grid dense: color does the separating work, so don't pad rows with airy whitespace to compensate for confidence in the design.
7. Any shadow beyond the FAB and truly floating/dragged elements (pickers, dropdowns) is over-scoped — the board itself stays flat.
8. Tabular numerals only for the Numbers column, dates and percentages — regular figures elsewhere.
9. Every status/label/group color must be re-mappable from the full multicolor set — never hardcode which hue means what beyond the default green/orange/red status set.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Forgeboard" — an internal ops tracker]
- Primary object being tracked: [e.g. "deals", "tickets", "sprints"]
- Number of default status values and their meaning: [e.g. 4: Not Started / In Progress / Blocked / Done]
- Columns needed beyond Status: [e.g. Owner, Priority, Due Date, Estimate]
- Views required: [e.g. Table + Kanban only, or all five]
- Brand accent color if different from monday.com blue: [hex or "keep #0073EA"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Any column-color constraints (e.g. must match an existing CRM's status set): [describe or "none"]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (SwiftUI `Color`/`Font` extensions or CSS variables) covering canvas, surfaces, text, the multicolor data palette and the action blue, light + dark
2. The Board Item Row component: group stripe + item name + person avatar(s) + full-bleed status cell, with exact padding/height/radius values
3. The Status/Label picker component (a grid of solid color options) and its open/close motion spec
4. The Battery rollup component with its segment-proportion logic and animation timing
5. The Kanban card variant and the drag-between-columns interaction (lift shadow, drop settle, haptic)
6. A dark-mode note confirming which tokens invert and which (the data palette) must never change
7. A short QA checklist mapped to the house rules above so a reviewer can catch tint-chip or blue-misuse regressions before merge
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in reverse-engineering best-in-class productivity-app visual systems and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI. You treat every extracted color, size and font as a literal spec to implement, not a mood to approximate.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Notion's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- Canvas: pure white #FFFFFF (light) / charcoal #191919 (dark — NOT true black)
- Surface gray #F7F6F3 (sidebar, subtle elevation) / dark surfaces #202020, #2F2F2F
- Divider #EAECEC / dark #373737
- Text primary: warm dark gray #37352F (light, NOT pure black) / #E6E6E4 (dark)
- Text secondary #9B9A97 (used identically in both modes)
- Primary action: Notion Black #000000 (the "New page" button) — the app has NO brand accent hue
- Link blue #2E75CC (light) / #529CCA (dark)
- Nine pastel PAGE backgrounds (light): Gray #F1F1EF, Brown #F4EEEE, Orange #FAEBDD, Yellow #FBF3DB, Green #EDF3EC, Blue #E7F3F8, Purple #F6F3F9, Pink #FAF1F5, Red #FDEBEC
- Matching saturated CALLOUT/highlight text colors: Orange #D9730D, Yellow #DFAB01, Green #0F7B6C, Blue #0B6E99, Purple #6940A5, Pink #AD1A72, Red #E03E3E

TYPE — three user-switchable families, never hardcode one:
- Inter (default sans), Lora (optional serif for quotes/literary notes), IBM Plex Mono (optional mono, code only)
- Ladder: Page Title 32pt/700, H1 24pt/700, H2 20pt/700, H3 16pt/700, Body 16pt/400, Code Inline/Block 14/13pt mono, Quote 17pt Lora italic

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; block vertical gap 6pt (tight reading rhythm); heading top margin 16pt; page content inset 16pt
- Radius scale: 0pt (dividers, covers), 4pt (callouts, code blocks, images, chips), 6pt (buttons, search, command palette), 12pt (sheets), 50% (avatars)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Block handle (⋮⋮⋮ drag + "+" insert) — 20pt glyphs in a 28pt hit area, invisible by default, revealed only on long-press (mobile, 400ms) or hover (desktop) — never always-visible
2. Slash ("/") command palette — a cursor-anchored 280pt floating panel, #FFFFFF bg, 1pt #EAECEC border, 6pt radius, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.08) 0 4px 12px, 40pt rows with icon+title+subtitle
3. Toggle block — leading ▸/▾ chevron rotating 90° over 150ms, children slide 0→auto height over 200ms, indented 24pt
4. Callout block — pastel background matched to a saturated text color, leading emoji, 16pt padding, 4pt radius, deliberately NO border
5. Mention chip — inline @-person/@-page with a 16pt avatar, 10% blue background (#2E75CC1A), 2pt radius, 2pt padding
6. Database block — one of six view modes (Table/Board/Timeline/Calendar/Gallery/List) switched via underlined tabs, all rendering the same underlying rows
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Block handles must default to invisible — surfacing them permanently defeats the entire "content is the interface" premise; they appear only on the defined hover/long-press trigger.
2. Never wrap a content block in a card border or drop shadow — Notion is flat by design; shadows exist only on floating panels (command palette, mention picker, bottom sheets).
3. Respect the active font-family setting globally — if the user has chosen Lora or IBM Plex Mono, every applicable surface honors it, not just one screen.
4. Page-background and callout pastels must stay desaturated/near-greyscale — a bright saturated fill here is off-system; save saturation for the paired TEXT color only.
5. Primary buttons stay Notion Black (or its dark-mode inversion) — do not introduce a colored brand CTA; the app deliberately has none.
6. Text primary is the warm gray #37352F, never #000000 — pure black reads as a different, colder product.
7. The "/" palette anchors to the text cursor position, not screen-center — a centered modal breaks the in-line editing feel.
8. Toggle and block-drag motion stays in the 150-300ms ease-out range — anything snappier reads as a different, more aggressive product register.
9. Mentions are always chips (avatar + tinted background), never plain colored inline text.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Fieldnote" — a research-wiki tool]
- Primary content unit: [e.g. "pages", "entries", "specs"]
- Block types needed at launch: [e.g. paragraph, heading, toggle, callout, image, checklist]
- Does the app need multiple type-family options, or is one sans sufficient?: [describe]
- Database/table views required: [e.g. Table + Board only, or all six]
- Brand accent, if any, beyond neutral black: [hex or "stay accent-free like Notion"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / React / Web]
- Collaboration features needed (mentions, comments, presence): [describe]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (light/dark, all nine pastel pairs, the three type families) as SwiftUI extensions or CSS variables
2. The block-handle component with its reveal trigger, hit-area size, and the drag-reorder + insert-below behaviors
3. The slash-command palette component: exact panel dimensions, row anatomy, keyboard/tap selection behavior, and open/close motion timing
4. Three worked block components for this project's chosen types (e.g. toggle, callout, database) with full styling
5. The mention-chip and page-icon/cover-hero patterns adapted to this project's content model
6. A dark-mode variance note — what inverts, what (mentions, callouts) needs re-paired contrast-safe colors
7. A short QA checklist enforcing "handles invisible by default" and "no card borders on content blocks" before merge
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity apps and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI, treating every extracted metric as a literal implementation spec rather than a stylistic suggestion.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Obsidian's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- Canvas #1E1E1E (deep charcoal, the default dark-workshop identity); light theme exists (#FFFFFF canvas, #1E1E1E text) but is secondary
- Surface steps: #262626 (panes, command palette body), #2D2D2D (modals, popovers, code blocks, hover rows), #363636 (pressed state, input fill, dividers)
- Text: primary #DCDDDE (soft off-white, not pure white), secondary #999999, tertiary/syntax-dimmed #6B6B6B
- Single connective accent: Obsidian Purple #7C3AED (primary action, active-file marker, blockquote bar, tag-pill base), lighter #A78BFA (wikilinks, active graph node, selection) — there is no second brand accent
- External links get a distinct cooler blue #7C9CBF (to visually separate from internal wikilinks)
- Semantic: success #4ADE80, error #F87171, highlight wash rgba(255,213,79,0.25) for ==text==

TYPE — a deliberate dual system, never collapse it to one font:
- Inter 400/600/700 for chrome, file rows, and the reading view
- JetBrains Mono 400/600 for the raw markdown source editor, code blocks, and the command palette
- Ladder: Note Title 26pt/700, Editor H1 24pt/700, Editor H2 20pt/700, Reading Body 16pt/400 (line-height 1.6), Source Body 15pt mono/400 (line-height 1.55), Pane Title 11pt/700 uppercase, Command Row 14pt mono

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; 16pt editor side padding; panes inset 12pt; file-tree rows touch with 0pt gap, depth communicated by 16pt indent steps
- Radius scale: 0pt (dividers, full-bleed editor), 6pt (buttons, code blocks, tab accents), 10pt (command palette, modals), 500pt (tag pills), 50% (graph nodes, avatars)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Graph view — a full-bleed physics-driven node/edge diagram; node radius scales 4-14pt with link count, active note glows #A78BFA with a purple halo, edges are 1pt #363636 brightening to purple near the focused node; continuous gentle drift, re-settling over ~600ms on drag or filter change
2. Backlinks pane ("Linked mentions") — a #262626 panel listing every note referencing the current one, each row showing the source title plus a context snippet with the matched link highlighted in #A78BFA
3. Markdown source editor with live syntax — monospace lines where `#`, `**`, `[[` render dimmed (#6B6B6B) but stay visible; wikilinks are tappable purple, external links a cooler blue
4. Command palette — a 560pt centered panel, #262626 bg, 1pt #363636 border, 10pt radius, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.6) 0 20px 56px, monospace rows with trailing keyboard-shortcut hints
5. Tag pills as graph connections — `#tag` rendered as a purple-tinted pill (rgba(124,58,237,0.14) bg, #A78BFA text), tapping filters the graph, not just cosmetic metadata
6. File-tree row — 32pt tall, 16pt-per-depth indent, active file marked by a 2pt purple left bar plus a tinted row background
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Purple (#7C3AED / #A78BFA) is the ONE connective accent across the entire app — never introduce a second brand hue; every purple instance should mean "this is a link, action, or focused node."
2. Markdown syntax characters in the source editor stay dimmed-but-VISIBLE (#6B6B6B) — hiding them entirely breaks the "you are always editing text" contract this app is built on.
3. Maintain the dual-font split without exception: Inter never appears in the source editor or command palette, and JetBrains Mono never appears in the reading view or chrome.
4. Elevation between panes is a charcoal color STEP (#1E1E1E → #262626 → #2D2D2D) plus a 1pt divider, not a drop shadow — reserve real shadows for genuinely floating surfaces like the command palette and context menus.
5. Graph node motion is a continuous gentle drift, never a snap or jump cut — dragging or filtering should feel like disturbing a real physical simulation.
6. There is no bottom tab bar — navigation lives in the left ribbon plus slide-over file-tree/backlinks/graph panes; do not introduce tab-bar chrome to "fit iOS conventions."
7. Tags render as first-class purple pills that filter the graph on tap — never demote them to plain gray metadata text.
8. Keep weights to Inter 400/600/700 and JetBrains Mono 400/600 only — no light or black weights anywhere; this is a utilitarian tool, not an editorial brand.
9. Backlinks must show a context snippet with the matched link highlighted, not just a bare list of note titles — the snippet is what makes the pane useful for "reading" the graph.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Loomwork" — a research/PKM tool]
- Primary content unit: [e.g. "notes", "entries", "specimens"]
- Does the app need a graph/relationship view, or just linear notes?: [describe]
- Markdown feature set required: [e.g. wikilinks, tags, highlights, blockquotes, code]
- Should tags act as graph nodes, or stay metadata-only?: [describe]
- Brand accent, if different from Obsidian purple: [hex or "keep #7C3AED"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / Electron / Web]
- Command-palette / keyboard-first requirements: [describe]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (dark-first, light variant, dual Inter/JetBrains Mono setup) as SwiftUI extensions or CSS variables
2. The graph-view component: node/edge rendering, the active-node halo, and the physics-drift/re-settle behavior spec
3. The backlinks ("Linked mentions") pane component with its context-snippet highlighting logic
4. The markdown source-editor line renderer: syntax dimming, wikilink/external-link coloring, and the reading/source toggle transition
5. The command palette component with exact dimensions, row anatomy, and open/close motion timing
6. A tag-pill component wired to filter the graph or search on tap
7. A short QA checklist enforcing "one accent only," "syntax stays visible," and "no second font leaking across surfaces" before merge
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity apps and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI, where every extracted color, spacing and timing value is a literal spec, never a rough approximation.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Things 3's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- Canvas #FFFFFF (pure white, protected by generous whitespace); dark mode exists (#1C1C1E canvas, #2C2C2E surface) but light is the primary identity
- Surface 1 #F5F6F8 (barely-there lift), Surface 2 / divider #ECECEC (whisper-thin)
- Text: primary #1D1D1F (near-black ink, not pure black), secondary #8A8A8E, tertiary #C7C7CC (also the completed-strikethrough color)
- Things Blue #4F97FF: the ONLY action/selection color — primary CTA, Magic-Plus, checkbox fill, links (pressed #3D7FE0)
- Today Yellow #FFD60A: the single other accent, reserved exclusively for the Today-list star and scheduled-today markers
- Semantic: Deadline Red #FF3B30 (overdue only)

TYPE — SF Pro (Display ≥20pt, Text below), weights 400/600/700 only, no light/black:
- List Title (Large) 28pt/700 with +0.3pt tracking ("feels like a chapter heading"), Section Heading 17pt/700, Task Title 17pt/400 (line-height 1.35), Body/Notes 15pt/400, Tiny Label 12pt/700 uppercase (e.g. "THIS EVENING")

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; 20pt horizontal margins (wider than the typical 16pt — deliberate part of the calm); 0pt gap between to-do rows (dividers + whitespace carry rhythm)
- Radius scale: 0pt (dividers), 8pt (selected-row highlight, segmented controls), 10pt (search field, filled buttons), 14pt (bottom sheets), 50% (checkbox, Magic-Plus, pie-progress ring)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Circular checkbox — 22pt diameter, 1.5pt border when unchecked; on completion fills #4F97FF center-out over ~180ms while a white checkmark springs in (response 0.3, damping 0.6), then the row fades + collapses out
2. Magic-Plus — a 56pt floating blue "+" that can be tapped to add a to-do at the top, OR press-and-dragged with a blue insertion line tracking the finger to drop a new to-do exactly between existing rows
3. Project pie-progress — an 18-22pt circular ring, #ECECEC track + #4F97FF fill arc proportional to completed to-dos, animating the arc forward (~300ms) whenever a to-do completes
4. Section headings inside a project — bold 17pt label + a thin #ECECEC hairline divider that chunks a long project into calm, collapsible sections
5. "This Evening" sub-section — inside the Today list, a small uppercase label separates evening-scheduled tasks from the rest of the day
6. Today star toggle — an 18pt star glyph, outline #C7C7CC when off, filled #FFD60A when on, with a quick 1.0→1.15→1.0 bounce on tap
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Things Blue is the ONLY action/selection color — never introduce a second brand accent; the Today-yellow star is the single deliberate exception, and it means "today" and nothing else.
2. Protect the whitespace: do not compress the 20pt margins or the roomy row heights to fit more content — density is explicitly not the goal here, unlike most task apps.
3. Completion must never be abrupt — the checkbox fill-and-spring-check, followed by a fade-and-collapse, is the signature delight and cannot be replaced with an instant state change.
4. The app stays almost entirely flat — the ONLY meaningful shadow anywhere is the soft blue glow under the Magic-Plus button; sheets get a gentle, low-opacity shadow at most.
5. There is no bottom tab bar — navigation is a sidebar (Inbox / Today / Upcoming / Anytime / Someday); introducing tab-bar chrome breaks the calm, single-surface feel.
6. Don't color-code tags or projects by default — color in this system is reserved for state (blue = action, yellow = today), not for decorative categorization.
7. Modal scrims stay unusually light (~0.2 opacity) — a heavy dimming layer reads as alarming, which is the opposite of the brand's calm register.
8. Section headings inside a project are a bold 17pt label plus a hairline divider — never a filled bar or colored background; the calm comes from restraint, not emphasis.
9. Weight stack is strictly 400/600/700 — no light weights anywhere, even though the overall feel is soft and quiet.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Driftlist" — a personal task planner]
- Primary unit being tracked: [e.g. "to-dos", "habits", "errands"]
- Core lists needed: [e.g. Inbox / Today / Upcoming / Someday, or a custom set]
- Does the app need a project/area hierarchy with progress tracking?: [describe]
- Brand accent, if different from Things Blue: [hex or "keep #4F97FF"]
- Is a single secondary accent (like the Today star) wanted, and for what state?: [describe or "none"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Creation gesture preference: [tap-only add, or Magic-Plus-style drag-to-insert]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (light + dark, the single blue accent plus the one yellow exception) as SwiftUI extensions or CSS variables
2. The to-do row component with the circular checkbox and its full fill-spring-collapse completion animation sequence
3. The Magic-Plus (or renamed equivalent) component covering both tap-to-add and press-drag-to-insert behaviors
4. The project pie-progress ring component with its arc-animation trigger logic
5. The section-heading + hairline-divider pattern adapted to this project's content hierarchy
6. A sidebar navigation layout (no tab bar) mapped to this project's core lists
7. A short QA checklist enforcing "whitespace stays generous," "blue is the only action color," and "completion is never abrupt" before merge
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity apps and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI, implementing every extracted value as a literal spec rather than an inspirational reference.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Todoist's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- Canvas #FFFFFF; Surface Gray #FAFAFA (sidebar, section headers); Divider #EEEEEE (0.5pt hairlines)
- Text: Ink #202020 (primary, slightly warm — never pure black), Secondary #808080, Tertiary/completed-strike #B0B0B0
- Todoist Red #DC4C3E: reserved strictly for VERBS — the brand mark, the floating "+" FAB, the P1 priority flag, primary CTAs — never ambient decoration or row backgrounds (pressed #B53C30)
- Four-tier priority system: P1 Red #DC4C3E, P2 Orange #EB8909, P3 Blue #246FE0, P4 transparent/gray-outline #808080
- A fixed 20-swatch project-color palette (Berry Red #B8255F, Orange #FF9933, Olive Green #AFB83B, Teal #158FAD, Grape #884DFF, Charcoal #808080, etc.) used only for project/label color dots
- Semantic: Success Green #058527 (today date pill), Error Red #D1453B

TYPE — SF Pro Display (≥20pt) / SF Pro Text (body/rows), weights 400/500/600/700, no custom face:
- Large Nav Title 34pt/700, Task Content 16pt/400 (the main row text), Section Header 13pt/600 UPPERCASE with 0.6pt tracking (e.g. "OVERDUE", flips to red for that section), Date Metadata 13pt/400 (color-codes: green=today, red=overdue, gray=future)

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; 16pt horizontal margin (24pt on iPad); rows touch with 0pt gap (hairline dividers carry rhythm, not whitespace) — this is one of the DENSEST task-app layouts by design
- Radius scale: 0pt (row backgrounds), 4pt (smart-parsing chips), 8pt (buttons, quick-add input, date-picker cells), 12pt (bottom sheets), 16pt (quick-add card top corners), 500pt (chips, count badges), 50% (checkboxes, project dots, FAB)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Task row — 52pt minimum, edge-to-edge, 22pt circular checkbox whose STROKE color (not the row background) signals priority: red/orange/blue/gray outline when empty, solid priority-color fill with a white check on completion
2. FAB with a tinted shadow — the 56pt red FAB's shadow is rgba(220,76,62,0.35) 0 6px 16px, a RED-tinted shadow rather than generic black — one of the most-copied details in the app
3. Quick-add card — a natural-language input ("buy milk tomorrow at 6pm p1 #home") that surfaces inline smart-parsing chips as you type: date matches become a blue chip, "p1" becomes a red priority chip, "#project" becomes a tinted project chip with its color dot
4. Priority flag glyph — a 14pt flag icon color-coded to the four-tier system, appearing in swipe actions and the quick-add metadata bar
5. Karma flame + streak — a small gradient flame (#FFB400 base to #DC4C3E tip) with an 800ms ember pulse, confined to the profile screen, never the task list
6. Sub-task tree lines — a 1pt #EEEEEE vertical line connecting indented sub-tasks to their parent checkbox
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Todoist Red is reserved exclusively for verbs — the FAB, the brand mark, the P1 flag, and primary CTAs — never for ambient decoration, row backgrounds, or non-priority accents.
2. Priority is communicated through the checkbox STROKE color, never through a tinted row background — the row itself is always plain white.
3. The FAB's shadow must be tinted red (rgba(220,76,62,0.35) 0 6px 16px), not a generic black drop-shadow — this is one of the most recognizable details in the system and a black shadow here is a visible regression.
4. Use the system font (SF Pro Display/Text) without exception — introducing a custom display face contradicts the deliberate "native iOS citizen" positioning.
5. Task rows stay dense: 52pt minimum height, edge-to-edge, separated by 0.5pt hairlines rather than vertical whitespace gaps — don't loosen this to "breathe more," density is the intended feel.
6. Keep karma/streak/gamification elements confined to the profile screen — they never appear on the task list or home screen.
7. The project-color system is a fixed palette (roughly 20 swatches) — don't let users pick arbitrary hex values; recognizability across a user's projects depends on the fixed set.
8. Completed tasks get a strikethrough plus a color shift to tertiary gray (#B0B0B0), then a 250ms collapse-upward animation — never an instant disappearance.
9. Section headers ("TODAY", "OVERDUE") are always 13pt/600 uppercase with 0.6pt tracking; the "OVERDUE" header alone flips to red — no other section header may use an accent color.
</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Priority levels needed: [e.g. Todoist's 4-tier P1-P4, or a simpler 3-tier]

name: Trello Design System
summary: Generate a SwiftUI implementation of Trello's board-first kanban system — the colored backdrop, drag-lift shadow and functional label palette.
description: A deep-research prompt that reproduces Trello's tactile, backdrop-driven kanban board as paste-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, from the navy-tinted drag shadow to the card detail sheet.

whatYouGet: A Trello-accurate token set built around the board BACKGROUND as the screen's canvas, plus the pale-list/white-card structure that keeps content readable on any backdrop
Full specs for the two hero components — the draggable card (with its navy-tinted lift shadow) and the horizontally-scrolling list column
A functional label-color system brief so the one place Trello lets color run free is implemented as data, not decoration
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity apps and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI, where every extracted metric becomes a literal build spec.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Trello's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- There is NO fixed canvas color — the board BACKGROUND (solid, gradient, or photo) sets the entire screen; default classic board blue is #0079BF, treated as a backdrop, not an action color
- Action blue #0C66E4 (pressed #0055CC) is the ONLY interactive color — CTAs, links, active tab, focus ring
- List surface #F1F2F4 (pale, floats on the backdrop); card fill #FFFFFF; divider #DFE1E6
- Text: primary #172B4D (deep navy-charcoal, not black), secondary #5E6C84, tertiary #8993A4; on-board text is white with a scrim behind photo backdrops
- Card label palette (the one FREE color zone, used as functional tags not decoration): Green #4BCE97, Yellow #F5CD47, Orange #FEA362, Red #F87168, Purple #9F8FEF, Blue #579DFF — each with a paler "subtle" variant for expanded chips
- Shadows use a NAVY tint rgba(9,30,66,…) rather than black, so they read on both colored backdrops and pale surfaces

TYPE — system font (SF Pro / Inter), weights 400/600/700, compact 11-24pt range:
- Board Name 20pt/700 (on-backdrop, white), List Title 15pt/600, Card Title 15pt/600 (up to ~4 lines), Body 15pt/400, Label (upper) 11pt/700 with 0.4pt tracking

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; list width ~272pt with 8pt gaps; board horizontal padding 8pt; card internal padding 8pt/12pt
- Radius scale: 4pt (label bars, tiny chips), 8pt (cards, buttons, inputs — Trello buttons are ROUNDED RECTS, never full pills), 12pt (list columns), 16pt (card detail sheet top corners), 50% (avatars)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Card drag-lift — on pick-up, scale 1.0→1.03 while the shadow ramps from a whisper rest state to rgba(9,30,66,0.25) 0 12px 24px over ~120ms; the source slot collapses and a placeholder gap opens at the destination, settling with a ~220ms spring on drop
2. Board-background header — the board's own backdrop (color/gradient/photo) bleeds behind the header and lists, with a subtle dark scrim on photos so white content stays legible; this backdrop IS the board's identity
3. Label row — a fixed six-color functional palette shown as compact 8pt bars across the card top, or expanded into full text chips inside card detail — the one deliberate exception to Trello's otherwise neutral-ink color discipline
4. Card detail sheet — a bottom sheet (16pt top-corner radius) presenting title/description/checklist(with a progress bar)/activity over a dimmed board (rgba(0,0,0,0.4) scrim)
5. Horizontal Kanban with no bottom tab bar — lists scroll left-to-right as the primary navigation surface; app-level navigation (Boards/Home/Notifications) lives in a top bar or drawer instead
6. Inline card composer — tapping "+ Add a card" expands a white multiline field with a blue "Add card" button in place, keeping focus for rapid sequential entry
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never impose a fixed canvas color — the board's own background (solid/gradient/photo) IS the screen; a hardcoded neutral app-wide background contradicts the entire system.
2. Card titles stay navy ink (#172B4D) regardless of how vivid the backdrop is — legibility over any background is the point of the white-card-on-colored-board structure.
3. Action blue (#0C66E4) is reserved for CTAs/links/active state; the classic board blue (#0079BF) is a BACKDROP default, never treated as an interactive color.
4. Shadows use the navy tint rgba(9,30,66,…), never pure black — this is what lets the same shadow read correctly on both pale lists and saturated board colors.
5. The card label palette is the one place color runs free, and only as functional tags (bars or chips) — never apply a label color to card TITLE text.
6. There is no bottom tab bar — Trello's primary navigation is the horizontally-scrolling board itself plus a top bar; adding tab-bar chrome contradicts the "board is the surface" premise.
7. Buttons are 8pt rounded rects, never full pills — this is a deliberate visual distinction from apps (like Todoist or Things) that use pill-shaped CTAs.
8. The drag-lift must be dramatic, not subtle — scale 1.03 plus a strong shadow jump communicates "picking up a physical object," and a barely-visible lift undersells the interaction.
9. Apply a scrim over photo board-backgrounds specifically (not solid-color ones) so white lists/cards/header text keep sufficient contrast.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Rowhouse" — a home-renovation project tracker]
- Primary unit being tracked: [e.g. "cards", "jobs", "content pieces"]
- Does each board/workspace need a customizable backdrop (color/photo), or one fixed brand color?: [describe]
- Number of default label colors needed: [e.g. Trello's 6, or a custom count]
- List/column structure: [e.g. fixed stages like To Do/Doing/Done, or user-defined]
- Brand accent, if different from Trello's action blue: [hex or "keep #0C66E4"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Card detail contents needed: [e.g. checklist, comments, attachments, due dates]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (backdrop defaults, list/card surfaces, the six-color label palette, navy-tinted shadow scale) as SwiftUI extensions or CSS variables
2. The Card component with its label row, title, badge row, and the full drag-lift/drop-settle animation sequence
3. The List/Column component with its header, vertical card stack, and inline "+ Add a card" composer
4. The board-level layout: horizontal list scroll, on-backdrop header treatment, and the photo-backdrop scrim rule
5. The Card Detail sheet with its checklist progress bar and activity section, scoped to this project's fields
6. A short QA checklist enforcing "no fixed canvas," "navy-tinted shadows only," and "label colors never touch title text" before merge
</what_to_give_me>

name: Zoom Design System
summary: Generate a SwiftUI implementation of Zoom's call-first system — the committed dark theater, active-speaker border and auto-hiding control bar.
description: A deep-research prompt that reproduces Zoom's "stage and crew" video-call UI as paste-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, from the gallery grid to the disciplined blue/red accent system.

whatYouGet: A Zoom-accurate token set covering the dual light/dark outside-call appearance and the committed dark theater used inside every meeting
Full specs for the gallery video tile (name chip, mute badge, active-speaker border) and the floating auto-hiding in-call control bar
A strict two-accent discipline brief — blue for action, red for leave/mute only — so the interface never blurs urgency with routine navigation
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in reverse-engineering the visual systems of best-in-class productivity and communication apps and rebuilding them faithfully in SwiftUI, implementing every extracted value as a literal spec rather than a loose inspiration.
</role>

<reference_data>
Extracted facts from Zoom's iOS visual language:

COLOR ROLES
- Outside a call: dual appearance, #FFFFFF (light) / #1A1A1A (dark) canvas
- INSIDE a call: the app commits unconditionally to the dark theater #1A1A1A, regardless of the user's system appearance setting, so participant video stays the brightest thing on screen
- Surfaces (dark) #2D2D2D (cards, control bar) / #3A3A3A (popovers, tile placeholders); light surface #F5F5F5
- Text (dark) primary #FFFFFF, secondary #B0B0B0, tertiary #7A7A7A; (light) primary #1A1A1A, secondary #6B6B6B
- Zoom Blue #2D8CFF: the SINGLE accent — Join/Start button, active controls, links, selected tab (pressed #1F6FCC)
- In-call red #E02828: reserved EXCLUSIVELY for Leave/End and the muted-microphone state — never used elsewhere
- Raise-hand yellow #F5C518 (reaction badge only); recording/warning use the same red / #F5A623 amber

TYPE — Lato/Inter approximation, weights 400/600/700, compact 10-28pt range, tabular numerics on timers/IDs:
- Screen Title 28pt/700, Meeting Topic 22pt/700 (the ceiling for display type — no heavier headline exists anywhere), List Title 16pt/600, Tile Name Label 13pt/600 (deliberately small so faces dominate), Call Timer 14pt/600 tabular, Tab Label 10pt/600

SPACING & RADIUS
- Base unit 4pt; 16pt standard horizontal margin; gallery tile GAP is a tight 4pt (maximize face size, minimize chrome)
- Radius scale: 0pt (dividers, full-bleed stage), 8pt (buttons, video tiles, inputs), 10-12pt (search fields, self-preview, sheets), 16pt (in-call control bar, modals — floating-card feel), 500pt (Join pill, chat composer), 50% (avatars, send button, mute badge bg)

NAMED DISTINCTIVE PATTERNS
1. Gallery video tile — 16:9, 8pt radius, a bottom-left name chip (13pt/600 white over rgba(0,0,0,0.45)) and a mic-mute badge (16pt red glyph on a dark circle); placeholder is a centered circular avatar when video is off
2. Active-speaker highlight — a 3pt #2D8CFF inset border that fades+scales onto whoever is talking, DEBOUNCED ~300ms so it never flickers between people, with only one tile highlighted at a time
3. In-call control bar — a floating 72pt bar, #2D2D2D at 96% opacity, 16pt radius, shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.4) 0 8px 24px, six evenly-spaced controls (Mute/Video/Share/Participants/React/Leave) that auto-hides after ~4s idle and restores on any tap of the video stage (200ms spring)
4. Oversized Join button — 48pt tall, 17pt/700 text — deliberately larger than any other button in the app so its SIZE alone is the primary-action affordance
5. Recording indicator — a pulsing red dot (scale 1.0↔0.7 over a 1.2s loop) beside an "RECORDING" uppercase label, top-left
6. Reactions tray — a slide-up emoji tray plus a Raise-Hand toggle; raised-hand renders a yellow badge on the tile, emoji reactions float up and fade over ~3s
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Inside a call the canvas is ALWAYS the dark theater #1A1A1A, overriding the user's system light/dark preference — video content must stay the brightest element on screen, full stop.
2. Blue (#2D8CFF) and red (#E02828) are the app's only two accents, and their meanings never blur: blue is always primary-action/active-state, red is always Leave/End or muted-microphone — never repurpose red for a generic error or warning.
3. The Join/Start button is deliberately oversized (48pt tall) — do not standardize it to match other button heights; its size is the intended affordance for "this is the one thing to tap."
4. Gallery tile name labels stay small (13pt, clamp at 15pt even with Dynamic Type) — the gallery is about faces, and text must never compete with them for visual weight.
5. The active-speaker border must be debounced (~300ms) — an un-debounced implementation will flicker rapidly between speakers in a multi-person conversation, which reads as broken rather than responsive.
6. The in-call control bar auto-hides after ~4 seconds of inactivity and restores on any tap of the video stage — a permanently-visible control bar is a deviation, not a simplification.
7. Use tabular numerics for the call timer and meeting IDs without exception — a reflowing timer digit is a visible defect during a live call.
8. Grid reflows (participants joining/leaving) animate over ~300ms ease-in-out — never snap instantly, which would be jarring mid-conversation.
9. Outside of a call, both light and dark appearance are fully supported and follow system preference; only the in-call surface is forced dark regardless of that setting.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name/product: [e.g. "Huddle" — a team video-call app]
- Core call surfaces needed: [e.g. gallery grid, speaker view, screen share]
- Max participants to support per gallery layout: [e.g. up to 9-up, or higher]
- Non-call surfaces needed: [e.g. meeting list, chat, contacts]
- Brand accent(s), if different from Zoom's blue/red pair: [hex(es) or "keep #2D8CFF / #E02828"]
- Platform target: [SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Reaction/raise-hand features required: [describe or "none"]
- Recording indicator required?: [yes/no]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color + Font token file (dual outside-call appearance, forced in-call dark theater, the strict two-accent set) as SwiftUI extensions or CSS variables
2. The Gallery Video Tile component with its name chip, mute badge, and active-speaker border (including the debounce logic)
3. The In-Call Control Bar component with its auto-hide/restore behavior and evenly-spaced control layout
4. The oversized Join/Start button component and the pre-meeting/join screen layout
5. A meeting-list row component for the non-call surface, scoped to this project's needs
6. The recording-indicator and/or reactions-tray component if requested in the project fields
7. A short QA checklist enforcing "in-call is always dark," "red means only leave/mute," and "the active-speaker border never flickers" before merge
</what_to_give_me>
